name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+40 partisan lean makes a Democratic win overwhelmingly likely
Democrat Chris Rabb has raised $1.3M with $1.6M in outside support versus $10.8K for the independent
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%
Open seat removes incumbency but does not threaten the seat's fundamental partisanship
model.rationale: This Philadelphia-area seat's D+40 fundamentals make it one of the most Democratic districts in the country, and the open-seat transition does not change that. Rabb's roughly 100-to-1 fundraising advantage over the token independent opposition and near-certain market pricing confirm the seat stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: A surprise primary upset or an unexpectedly well-funded independent consolidation could tighten things, but no realistic path exists for the opposition here.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Dwight Evans is retiring from a Philadelphia-based district with a D+40 partisan lean, one of the most Democratic seats in Pennsylvania. State Representative Chris Rabb enters as the heavy favorite on the Democratic side, having raised about $1.3 million and drawn roughly $1.6 million in outside support. The only general-election opponent is independent Dennis Mahoney, who has raised about $10,800 with no outside backing.

Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no polling available, the forecast rests on the district's overwhelming fundamentals and the lopsided resource gap, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
